EXPRESSION OF THE PROPERTIES OF CATHODE-RAY OSCILLOSCOPES
PART 2 STORAGE OSCILLOSCOPES

National Foreword

This Indian Standard (Part 2), which is identical with IEC Pub 351-2 (1976) `Expression of the properties of cathode-ray oscilloscopes, Part 2 : Storage oscilloscopes', issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on the recoInmendation of the Electronic Measuring Equipment Sectional Committee and .approved by the Electronics and Telecomnunication Division Council.

1. General This standard should be used in conjunction of Cathode-ray Oscilloscopes, Part 1: General. with I EC Publication 351-l. Expression of the Properties

1.I .l This standard applies to storage oscilloscopes with special devices incorporated in the cathode-ray tube permuting the recording of a signal in another way than by the ability of the screen coating to ensure persistence of the display of information. 1.1.2 This standard does not apply to oscilloscopes with a normal tube and storage devices external to the tube. However, some clauses of the standard may be applied with agreement between the manufacturer and tl!e usei 1.1.3 This standard does not apply to oscilloscopes which have a cathode-ray with long persistence which temporarily retains the display. tube having a screen

1.1.4 Certain `types of storage oscilloscopes are capable of operation without storage. When so operated, Publication 351-l applies directly. In this standard. it is assumed that the oscilloscope is operated, unless otherwise stated. as a storage oscilloscope.

Object

3. Requirements and test methods

General: I) Since most of the performance characteristics that follow arc closely related to each other and depend a great deal on the individual settings of the control knobs. it is mandatory to Icavc all the controls at their preliminary settings while performing the tests specified in Sub-clauses 3.1 to 3.9 in sequence. Preliminary setting of the controls is carried out by successive ~lpproxilllilli0n 10 ilCl)iWC optimum overall storage performance. When this is achieved. the settings of the controls and the results of the iests correspond to the normal usage of the storage oscilloscope: consequently. the figures ohtaincd for the performance characteristics will not necessarily be the maximum possible values.

2) If, in addition, the manufacturer wishes to specify the maximum obtainable figures for any one ol the characteristics given in Sub-clauses 3.1 to 3.9, he is entitled to do so. This may require different individual control settings for the measurement of each characteristic. and if so. this shall be clearly stated. 3) Ambient illumination &all be negligibly low in order not to affect luminance mcasuremcnts. may wish to

The same test procedure is to be follotved as described in Sub-clause 3.1. but additionally a clock is started at the moment of triggering the single sweep. 3.5

Checking qf the retention time

The same test procedure is to be followed as described in Sub-clause 3.1. Immediately after the single sweep ends, the oscilloscope is switchect to `"stored'" mode of operation and a clock is started. After the time specified -by the manufacturer. the oscilloscope is switched to "display'" tlmde of operation. Compliance is met if the display shows none of the defects described in Sub-clause 3.4.
